sections.title: What it really costs
sections.intro: Monthly running costs, how the fees compare, and the one-off costs of buying.

items.head: Repair fund ¥16,800/month = ¥140/m²
items.detail: MLIT guideline for a building like this (under 20 floors, floor area < 5,000 m²): average ¥335/m², ⅔ of buildings ¥235–430. At the guideline average this flat would pay ≈ ¥40,207/month (+¥23,407). A fund below the guideline usually means future increases or a one-off levy (一時金).
items.cmp: Peers built ±5 years (289 watchlist condos): median ¥190/m², middle half ¥127–238 → this flat is at the 34th percentile.
items.ask: Please share the 長期修繕計画 and the current repair-fund balance. Are increases or a 一時金 planned?

items.head: Management fee ¥21,960/month = ¥183/m² (委託(常駐))
items.detail: Small buildings cost more per flat; staffed (常駐) management costs more than visiting (巡回).
items.cmp: Peers of similar age: median ¥179/m² → 55th percentile (289 condos)

items.head: ≈ ¥157,320/month before parking and property tax
items.detail: Loan ¥118,560 (100% of price, 35 years, 1.00% variable — the Apartments tab default) + fees ¥38,760
items.ask: What was the last 固定資産税・都市計画税 bill for this unit?

items.head: One-off buying costs ≈ ¥2,712,000–¥3,552,000
items.detail: Agent fee (仲介手数料, 3% + ¥60k + tax) ¥1,452,000 · plus registration tax and scrivener, loan fees and guarantee, fire + earthquake insurance, stamp duty, pro-rated property tax and fees: typically 3–5% of the price.

sections.title: Earthquake safety

items.head: Built 2013-03 — current seismic standard (新耐震)
items.detail: The rule depends on the building-permit date (from June 1981); completion from spring 1983 is almost always new-standard.

items.head: Structure: RC, 11 floors
items.detail: RC/SRC are the norm for condos.

items.head: 30-year chance of shaking ≥ 6-lower here: 54% (≥ 6-upper: 12%)
items.detail: ≥ 5-upper: 95%. Modern buildings are designed for this; the risk is contents, lifts, pipes and the days without water or power.
items.cmp: Study areas (population-weighted, ≥ 6-lower): median 59%, range 24–89% → rank 27 of 78 from the safest

items.head: Ground: 火山灰台地 — shaking amplified ×1.40
items.detail: Soft ground amplifies shaking (AVS30 269 m/s; about 1.6 or more counts as soft). Ask how the building is founded (piles to bearing stratum?).
items.ask: What kind of foundation does the building have (支持層までの杭基礎)?

src: J-SHIS 地震ハザードステーション

sections.title: Water and ground
sections.intro: Depth bands are the maximum assumed scenario (想定最大規模) at SUUMO's map point; SUUMO's point is approximate, so the worst value within ~100 m is shown too.

items.head: River flood: outside the mapped zone
Storm surge: outside the mapped zone
Liquefaction tendency: very low
items.detail: Landform: 切土地 on 台地･段丘 (国土地理院). Condo towers on piles usually stand, but roads, pipes, gas and sewers around them can fail for weeks (as in Urayasu 2011).

items.head: Area context (Inzai)
items.cmp: 15% of residents live in some water zone · 8% on high-liquefaction ground · 1.5% in landslide zones

items.head: Old maps
items.detail: Check what the site was before (sea, paddy, river) on 今昔マップ; past disaster records and 大規模盛土 maps come with the MLIT API key.

sections.intro: Yahoo!乗換案内, next Wednesday, arrive by 08:45, IC fare, no paid express. Door-to-door = access to the station + train + 5 min at the office end.

items.detail: MLIT peak-hour 混雑率 (150% = can read a newspaper folded; 180% = pressed together).

items.head: 1 different line(s) listed
items.detail: A second line is a fallback when one line stops (Keiyo line is often stopped by wind).

items.head: Management: 委託(常駐)
items.detail: 常駐 = resident manager, 日勤/通勤 = manager on weekdays.

items.head: Age 13 years — 1st major repair (外壁・屋上防水) due around now
items.detail: Major repairs come every ~12–15 years. Ask whether the last one was done on time and paid from the fund (not by a levy or loan).
items.ask: When was the last 大規模修繕, what did it cover and how was it paid? What is planned next?

items.head: Key documents decide this section

items.ask: Can I see the 重要事項調査報告書 and the last 2–3 years of 総会議事録?

items.head: Floor 6 of 11
items.detail: Middle floor: neighbours above and below insulate.

items.head: 120.02 m² (壁芯) ≈ 112.8 m² registered
items.detail: The tax rules (mortgage credit ≥ 50 m²) use the registered 内法 area, about 5–8% smaller than the advertised 壁芯 area.

sections.title: Energy, windows and running cost
sections.intro: Energy labels are only required for new buildings (from April 2024): used flats almost never show them, so proxies are used.

items.head: No energy label (normal for used flats)
items.ask: Is there a 住宅性能評価書, BELS or 長期優良住宅 certificate?

items.head: Likely designed to 1999 rules (次世代省エネ, ~today's 等級4)
items.detail: Era is only a hint: condos were not required to meet the energy standard until 2025.

items.head: Window type not stated
items.detail: In condos the window frames are common property: you usually cannot replace them yourself; inner windows (内窓) are allowed and subsidised.
items.ask: Are the windows single or double glazed? Were sashes replaced in a major repair?

items.head: Gas type not stated
items.detail: Propane (LPG) costs much more than city gas.
items.ask: City gas or propane? Electricity contract (high-voltage bulk 一括受電)?

items.head: Equipment: 省エネ給湯器, 床暖房
Mortgage tax credit: eligible
items.detail: Built 1982 or later ✓ · registered area ≥ 50 m² ✓. Without an energy certificate a used home falls in the basic tier: 0.7% of the loan balance up to ¥20M for 10 years (max ¥140k/year). With a 省エネ基準適合 certificate it is 13 years; ZEH-level / 長期優良 raises the cap to ¥35M.
